message: No detected input validation: No schema checks, dtype assertions, or value-range guards are applied to any incoming data; URLs and CSVs are loaded and used directly without validation.

No detected untrusted source handling: Remote data is fetched via plain HTTP (http://data.phishtank.com/data/online-valid.csv) and HTTPS without any checksum verification, signature validation, or pinned revision; only a bare exception catch for access denial is present.

No detected label flipping detection: The code assigns labels (0 for legitimate, 1 for phishing) directly without any validation, distribution comparison, or label-noise detection tool such as Cleanlab.

No detected data poisoning defenses: There are no outlier detection, statistical anomaly checks, or suspicious-input filtering steps applied to the collected URLs or extracted features before dataset construction.

No detected model integrity verification: The code loads serialized models (e.g., 'data/classifier.pkl', 'data/brands.pkl', 'data/words.pkl') via pickle.load/load without any hash check, signature verification, or pinned revision check.
No detected label distribution validation: There is no code that checks class balance, validates the expected label set, or detects anomalous training samples before training begins.
No detected backdoor or trigger detection: No neural-cleanse, activation-pattern analysis, gradient anomaly detection, or any other backdoor/trigger defense is present in the training code.
No detected differential privacy: There is no use of Opacus, TensorFlow Privacy, DP-SGD, or any other differential privacy mechanism in the code.
No detected adversarial robustness testing: No adversarial robustness testing frameworks (Foolbox, ART, FGSM, PGD) or any robustness stress tests are present in the code.

No detected metric tampering protection: There is no evidence of a held-out test set isolation from training, signed/hashed evaluation data, or use of multiple independent metrics to protect against metric manipulation.

No detected input sanitization: URLs are passed directly from CSV files or lists into the feature extractor and classifier without any shape/range checks, schema validation, or malformed input rejection.
No detected output bounds checks: No code is visible that checks model outputs for probability sanity bounds, NaN guards, or calibrated thresholds before returning predictions.

No detected prompt injection defenses: This is a URL/phishing classification pipeline using traditional ML models, not an LLM, so prompt injection defenses are not applicable and none are implemented.
